classification.difficultyReason: Interpret both plotted journeys and their speeds, then obtain an exact meeting time by using a common time origin, accounting for Albert's delayed departure, and equating distances from town A.

content.prompt: The following graph shows the distance from town A against time for two cyclists, Albert and Bob. Town B is 48 km from town A.

spec.description: Distance from town A against time. Albert travels from (1 p.m., 0 km) to (4 p.m., 48 km); Bob travels from (Noon, 48 km) to (4 p.m., 0 km). Both journeys are blue; red dashed reference guides identify 48 km and 4 p.m. No grid is printed.
spec.mathematics: With t hours after Noon, Albert has distance 16(t−1) for 1≤t≤4 and Bob has distance 48−12t for 0≤t≤4. Their intersection is t=16/7, d=144/7.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied journeys and reference guides remain visible; intersection coordinates and meeting time are not printed.

answer.worked: Albert travels from town A to town B, a distance of $48\text{ km}$.

Albert travels for $3$ hours, from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Albert's speed} &= \frac{48}{3}\\\text{Albert's speed} &= 16\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

Bob travels for $4$ hours, from Noon to 4 p.m.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bob's speed} &= \frac{48}{4}\\\text{Bob's speed} &= 12\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: How many hours after Noon do the two cyclists pass each other?

inlines.text: At the intersection, both cyclists have the same distance from town A.

answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the number of hours after Noon. At the intersection, the distances from town A are equal.
$$\begin{align*}16(t-1) &= 48-12t\\16t-16 &= 48-12t\\28t &= 64\\t &= \frac{16}{7}\text{ h}\end{align*}$$
They pass $\frac{16}{7}$ hours after Noon, equivalently $\frac{9}{7}$ hours after Albert starts.
